deep.reconstruction:
The page has two layers. Left column: a short computation. Right column and lower half: a heavily corrected draft of a personal letter, dated (crossed out) 'Göttingen, den Mai 1855' and signed 'B Riemann'. It mentions someone (probably Weber) having travelled 'am vorigen Donnerstag nach Marburg'. The letter has no mathematical content.

Mathematics (left column, top). Write A=(P,Q,R) for a vector field and u for a scalar function of x,y,z. Riemann writes:
(1) u_x + Q_z - R_y = 0
(2) u_y + R_x - P_z = 0
(3) u_z + P_y - Q_x = 0
(4) P_x + Q_y + R_z = 0. The right-hand side is hard to read and may run into the letter text; reading it as 0 fits the system.
In vector form, (1)-(3) say grad u = curl A, and (4) says div A = 0. This is a first-order system with one scalar and one vector unknown. It is the natural three-dimensional analogue of the Cauchy-Riemann equations u_x = v_y, u_y = -v_x: one scalar potential u is paired with a 'conjugate' vector potential A.

Consequences (implicit; supplied by me, certain):
- Taking the divergence of grad u = curl A gives Δu = div curl A = 0, so u is harmonic.
- Taking the curl gives 0 = curl grad u = curl curl A = grad div A - ΔA. With (4), each of P, Q, R is harmonic.

Riemann then writes the total differentials
dP = P_x dx + P_y dy + P_z dz and dQ = Q_x dx + Q_y dy + Q_z dz,
and the differentials of the gradient components, i.e. the Hessian of u acting on (dx,dy,dz):
- d(u_x) = u_xx dx + u_xy dy + u_xz dz
- d(u_y) = u_xy dx + u_yy dy + u_yz dz
- d(u_z) = u_xz dx + u_yz dy + u_zz dz
These are presumably preparation for changing variables, i.e. using u and the conjugate potentials as new coordinates. That is exactly what the next page does in the axially symmetric case.

The next page specialises to rotational symmetry: (r u_r)_r + r u_zz = 0, with Stokes' stream function w defined by r u_r = w_z, r u_z = -w_r. It then inverts to r(u,w), z(u,w) and looks for a complex combination dw + i r du. The link (mine) is this: if A is azimuthal, A = ψ(r,z) e_φ, then grad u = curl A gives u_r = -ψ_z and u_z = (1/r)(rψ)_r. Setting w = -rψ yields exactly r u_r = w_z, r u_z = -w_r. So this page is the general 3D 'conjugate function' system, and the next page is its axisymmetric reduction (scalar potential plus Stokes stream function).

The date 1855 and the axisymmetric potential problem fit Riemann's 1855 paper on Nobili's colour rings (Poggendorffs Annalen), which treats axially symmetric current flow. The connection is plausible but not certain.
errors: No substantive errors in the mathematics.
Slips in exponents: in the d(∂u/∂x) and d(∂u/∂y) rows some mixed second derivatives appear in the image as ∂u/∂x∂z or ∂u/∂y∂z, i.e. the superscript 2 is missing.
The right-hand side of the divergence equation (4) is illegible or entangled with the letter text. '=0' is an inference: it is what makes P, Q, R harmonic, but it is not certain from the image.

results.what: First-order system grad u = curl(P,Q,R), div(P,Q,R) = 0, as a 3D analogue of the Cauchy-Riemann equations (harmonic scalar with a conjugate harmonic vector)
results.modern_name: Moisil-Teodorescu system / Riesz system, the equation Df=0 for quaternion-valued (Fueter-monogenic) functions; physically, the scalar magnetic potential equals the curl of a solenoidal vector potential
results.usually_credited_to: Moisil & Teodorescu (1931), Fueter (1930s), M. Riesz (1950s) as function theory. The physical relation grad φ = curl A was known in 19th-century electrodynamics (F. Neumann, Weber, Kirchhoff, Helmholtz, Maxwell)

results.what: u harmonic and A harmonic follow from the system (implicit)
results.modern_name: div curl = 0, curl grad = 0, and the vector Laplacian identity

results.what: Total differentials of P, Q and of the components of grad u (Hessian of u)
results.modern_name: Chain rule / Jacobian and Hessian matrix

results.what: Reduction to the axisymmetric case with Stokes stream function (continued on the next page)
results.modern_name: Stokes stream function; axisymmetric potential theory (generalized axially symmetric potentials)
results.usually_credited_to: Stokes (1842); Beltrami (1880s) for the function-theoretic treatment

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann sets up a genuinely 3D Cauchy-Riemann-type system (scalar plus solenoidal vector potential), apparently as a step toward a function theory of axisymmetric potentials. The page is dated 1855 and probably connected to his Nobili rings work. The relation grad u = curl A was physically familiar. However, viewing it as the 3D generalisation of conjugate functions predates Beltrami, Moisil-Teodorescu and Fueter. The page itself derives nothing beyond writing the system and differentials, so the significance is modest.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); u=x*y; P=x*z; Q=-y*z; R=0; [simplify(diff(u,x)+diff(Q,z)-diff(R,y)), simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(R,x)-diff(P,z)), simplify(diff(u,z)+diff(P,y)-diff(Q,x)), simplify(diff(P,x)+diff(Q,y)+diff(R,z))] == [0,0,0,0]
checkable.asserts: A nontrivial solution of Riemann's system exists (u=xy, A=(xz,-yz,0)); consistency of the signs as written

checkable.sympy: u=z; P=-y/2; Q=x/2; R=0; [diff(u,x)+diff(Q,z)-diff(R,y), diff(u,y)+diff(R,x)-diff(P,z), diff(u,z)+diff(P,y)-diff(Q,x), diff(P,x)+diff(Q,y)+diff(R,z)] == [0,0,0,0]
checkable.asserts: A second simple solution: u=z with A=(-y/2,x/2,0)

checkable.sympy: P,Q,R=[Function(n)(x,y,z) for n in 'PQR']; ux=diff(R,y)-diff(Q,z); uy=diff(P,z)-diff(R,x); uz=diff(Q,x)-diff(P,y); simplify(diff(ux,x)+diff(uy,y)+diff(uz,z))==0
checkable.asserts: If grad u = curl A then Δu = 0 (div curl = 0)

checkable.sympy: r,z=symbols('r z',positive=True); psi=Function('psi')(r,z); w=-r*psi; ur=-diff(psi,z); uz=diff(r*psi,r)/r; [simplify(r*ur-diff(w,z)), simplify(r*uz+diff(w,r))]==[0,0]
checkable.asserts: With an azimuthal A = psi e_phi and w = -r psi, grad u = curl A reduces to the next page's r u_r = w_z, r u_z = -w_r
Integrability: the axisymmetric equation (r u_r)_r + r u_zz = 0 is the compatibility condition for the Stokes stream function w (the expression vanishes identically)

transcription_corrections: The right column is not 'Vor Kurzem musste ich...'; it is the continuation of a letter draft whose content cannot be reliably read. The mathematical part on the left is unaffected.
The right-hand side of the equation ∂P/∂x+∂Q/∂y+∂R/∂z may not read '=0'; it is partly obscured by or entangled with the letter text ('= ohne, ...'?). Mark it as uncertain.
In the image some second-derivative symbols lack the exponent 2, e.g. '∂u/∂x∂z dz' and '∂u/∂y∂z dz'. The transcription silently corrected these.

The salutation 'Liebster[?] ...!' is uncertain. The letter is dated 'Göttingen, den Mai 1855' (crossed out) and signed 'B Riemann'; 'Weber ist am vorigen Donnerstag nach Marburg gereist' appears plausible but the first word is uncertain.
